It provides a CLI, a REST API, and Python and JavaScript libraries, and can connect to existing agents and applications. The README describes macOS, Windows, Linux, and Docker installation, with llama.cpp listed as a supported backend.
title: Ollama

body: text-generation
plain_description: **Use OLMo to generate English text for language modeling and other applications.** The model is available for inference and fine-tuning. Check generated facts, as the README warns that they may be inaccurate.
technical_description: OLMo 7B is an autoregressive Transformer language model developed by the Allen Institute for AI and trained on the Dolma dataset. The README provides Hugging Face inference and fine-tuning instructions and describes model checkpoints and revisions. The code and model are released under Apache 2.0.
title: OLMo 7B

body: A coding agent for open models like Kimi K3.1 and GLM 5.3
plain_description: **Give your team a coding agent that works with low-cost models.** Switch between model providers and agent harnesses from the terminal. Use it with compatible editors and clients through ACP.
technical_description: A Rust-based coding agent forked from OpenAI Codex, designed to emulate agent harnesses for low-cost models. It runs in a terminal, supports multiple model providers and harnesses, native sandboxing on macOS, Linux, and Windows, and integrations including ACP, MCP, and the Codex exec protocol.
title: Open Interpreter

body: Open-Sora: Democratizing Efficient Video Production for All
plain_description: **Create high-quality videos from text prompts or reference images.** Generate and edit video at different resolutions, lengths, and aspect ratios. The project also provides tools for training and fine-tuning video models.
technical_description: Open-Sora is an open-source video generation project with text-to-video and image-to-video pipelines, video data preprocessing, inference, training, and fine-tuning. Its README describes an 11B model supporting 256px and 768px output, with single- and multi-GPU inference. Setup uses Python, PyTorch, CUDA-dependent xformers, and flash-attn; examples use H100/H800 GPUs.
title: Open-Sora

body: User-friendly AI Interface (Supports Ollama, OpenAI API, ...)
plain_description: **Give your team one place to use AI models.** Connect local models through Ollama or use OpenAI-compatible APIs for local and cloud models. Run it on your own setup, including offline.
technical_description: Open WebUI is an extensible, self-hosted AI platform that runs entirely offline. It connects to local models through Ollama and to local or cloud models through OpenAI-compatible APIs. The README documents Python and Docker installation, a native desktop app, and Kubernetes deployment guidance.
title: Open WebUI

body: Open3D: A Modern Library for 3D Data Processing
plain_description: **Build software for working with 3D data using Open3D’s C++ and Python tools.** Process and visualize 3D data, reconstruct scenes, and align surfaces. GPU acceleration and support for PyTorch and TensorFlow are available.
technical_description: Open3D is an open-source C++ and Python library for 3D data processing. It provides data structures and algorithms for scene reconstruction, surface alignment, visualization, physically based rendering, and 3D machine learning with PyTorch and TensorFlow. Core 3D operations support GPU acceleration.
title: Open3D: A Modern Library for 3D Data Processing

body: Open-source observability for your GenAI or LLM application, based on OpenTelemetry
plain_description: **See how your LLM application is performing and where issues occur.** Instrument LLM providers, vector databases, and frameworks to collect traces and other observability data. Send that data to supported monitoring tools such as Datadog, Grafana, or Honeycomb.
technical_description: OpenLLMetry is a set of OpenTelemetry extensions and a Traceloop SDK for observability in LLM applications. It provides instrumentations for LLM providers, vector databases, and frameworks, and exports standard OpenTelemetry data to supported observability destinations. The README says SDK and instrumentation telemetry collection was discontinued in version 0.49.2 and above.
title: OpenLLMetry

body: An Easy-to-use, Scalable and High-performance Agentic RL Framework based on Ray (PPO & DAPO & REINFORCE++ &  VLM & TIS & vLLM & Ray & Async  RL)
plain_description: **Train and refine language models with reinforcement learning from human feedback.** Run supervised fine-tuning, preference learning, reward-model training, and RL workflows with built-in algorithms and custom rewards. Scale training across GPUs and nodes.
technical_description: OpenRLHF is a Python framework for RLHF and agent-based reinforcement learning. It supports supervised fine-tuning, DPO/IPO/cDPO, reward-model training, and PPO, REINFORCE++, GRPO, RLOO, and related algorithms. It uses Ray for distributed scheduling, vLLM for generation, DeepSpeed for training, and Hugging Face Transformers for model loading and fine-tuning. Supports single- and multi-turn agents, custom rewards, LoRA/QLoRA, and multimodal VLM training.
title: OpenRLHF

body: OpenVINO™ is an open source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference
plain_description: **Optimize and deploy AI models across a range of devices, from edge to cloud.** Use models built with popular machine learning frameworks. Run inference on CPUs, Intel GPUs, and Intel NPUs.
technical_description: Open-source toolkit for optimizing and deploying deep learning models. It supports model conversion and inference with models from PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, TensorFlow Lite, PaddlePaddle, and JAX/Flax, and provides C++, Python, C, and Node.js APIs. The README describes CPU, Intel GPU, and Intel NPU inference, plus generative AI pipelines.
title: OpenVINO

body: Instant voice cloning by MIT and MyShell. Audio foundation model.
plain_description: **Clone a voice and create speech in multiple languages and accents.** Control emotion, accent, rhythm, pauses, and intonation. OpenVoice V1 and V2 are free for commercial use.
technical_description: OpenVoice is an audio foundation model for instant voice cloning. It can clone a reference voice’s tone color and generate speech across languages and accents, with controls for emotion, accent, rhythm, pauses, and intonation. V2 adds improved audio quality and native support for English, Spanish, French, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
title: OpenVoice

body: Turn any PDF or image document into structured data for your AI. A powerful, lightweight OCR toolkit that bridges the gap between images/PDFs and LLMs. Supports 100+ languages.
plain_description: **Turn PDFs and images into structured data your business can use.** Extract text and document details into JSON or Markdown, across more than 100 languages. Use the results to prepare information for AI and document workflows.
technical_description: PaddleOCR is an OCR toolkit and document AI engine for recognizing text and parsing documents. It converts PDFs and images to structured JSON or Markdown, supports multilingual recognition, and includes document parsing for tables, formulas, charts, and other elements. The README describes local inference, browser inference, service deployment, and integrations with tools such as Dify and RAGFlow.
title: PaddleOCR

body: Flexible and powerful data analysis / manipulation library for Python, providing labeled data structures similar to R data.frame objects, statistical functions, and much more
plain_description: **Analyze and organize business data with Python.** Work with labeled data, combine and reshape datasets, and load information from files and databases.
technical_description: pandas is a Python package for data analysis and manipulation. It provides labeled data structures, missing-data handling, alignment, grouping, merging, joining, reshaping, indexing, and time-series features. It includes tools for reading CSV, Excel, and database data and for storing data in HDF5.
title: pandas

body: Inference and training library for high-quality TTS models.
plain_description: **Create natural sounding speech from text and guide the voice’s style, pitch, and speaking rate.** Use an interactive demo or integrate speech generation into your workflow. The library also includes tools to train or fine-tune models.
technical_description: Parler-TTS is an open source Python library with inference and training code for text-to-speech models. It generates speech from text and natural language descriptions of voice characteristics, with named speakers available for more consistent voice selection. The repository documents installation, inference, training, and fine-tuning.
title: Parler-TTS

body: 🤗 PEFT: State-of-the-art Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning.
plain_description: **Adapt large pretrained models to your business tasks with less compute and storage.** PEFT fine-tunes a small number of extra parameters instead of changing the entire model. Its adapters can be used with Hugging Face Transformers, Diffusers, and Accelerate.
technical_description: PEFT is a Python library of parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for adapting pretrained models by training a small subset of additional parameters. It integrates with Transformers for training and inference, Diffusers for managing adapters, and Accelerate for distributed training and inference. Methods include LoRA and support combining PEFT with quantization.
title: 🤗 PEFT

body: Open-source vector similarity search for Postgres
plain_description: **Add fast similarity search to the Postgres data your business already stores.** Find nearby items with exact or approximate search, and combine vector queries with Postgres filters and full-text search.
technical_description: An open-source PostgreSQL extension for storing single-precision, half-precision, binary, and sparse vectors and querying nearest neighbors. Supports exact search and approximate search with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes, multiple distance metrics, binary quantization, and hybrid search with PostgreSQL full-text search. Works with any language that has a Postgres client.
title: pgvector

body: text-generation
plain_description: **Build English language features that can handle long documents, reasoning, and code with a compact model.** It supports up to 128K tokens of context. Developers can adapt it for specific applications, including through fine-tuning.
technical_description: A 3.8 billion-parameter, decoder-only Transformer language model trained for text generation and instruction following. It supports 128K-token context, is available through Hugging Face Transformers, and has ONNX variants for CPU, GPU, and mobile inference. The README provides a multi-GPU fine-tuning example.
title: Phi-3-Mini-128K-Instruct

body: text-generation
plain_description: **Help your team analyze images and understand the text alongside them.** Use it for image understanding, OCR, and chart or table analysis. It can run in compute constrained environments.
technical_description: Phi-3-Vision-128K-Instruct is a 4.2B parameter multimodal model that accepts text and image inputs and generates text responses. It supports a 128K-token context and is integrated with Transformers. The README recommends GPU use and lists NVIDIA A100, A6000, and H100 as tested hardware.
title: Phi-3.5 Vision Instruct

body: A fast, local neural text to speech system
plain_description: **Turn written text into speech with a fast, local text-to-speech system.**
technical_description: Piper is described in the repository metadata as a fast, local neural text-to-speech system. Development has moved to https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl.
title: Piper

body: An app that brings language models directly to your phone.
plain_description: **Give your team a private AI assistant that runs on a phone.** Chat with language models, use voice input and spoken replies, and create tailored assistants. Download a model once to use the app offline.
technical_description: PocketPal AI is an iOS and Android app for running GGUF language models on-device, with chat, personalized assistants, tool use, Whisper speech recognition, and text-to-speech. It supports CPU, GPU, and NPU inference, Hugging Face model downloads, and an optional local API server. Core chat works offline after downloading a model.
title: PocketPal AI

body: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames, written in Rust
plain_description: **Analyze and transform large datasets quickly with DataFrame queries or SQL.** Build expressive queries that run in parallel, and spill operations to disk when they exceed available RAM.
technical_description: Polars is an analytical query engine written in Rust for DataFrames and SQL. Both interfaces use the same optimizer and execution engine. It supports lazy queries, parallel and vectorized execution, disk spilling, NVIDIA GPU acceleration, and Apache Arrow data sharing. Available through Python, Rust, Node.js, and R.
title: Polars

body: An open-source framework for detecting, redacting, masking, and anonymizing sensitive data (PII) across text, images, and structured data. Supports NLP, pattern matching, and customizable pipelines.
plain_description: **Detect and de-identify sensitive information to help protect your organization’s data.** Presidio can identify and redact personal information in text and images. Customize detection rules for your business needs.
technical_description: An open-source framework for identifying and anonymizing personally identifiable information in text and images. It includes predefined and custom recognizers using named entity recognition, regular expressions, rules, checksums, and contextual analysis across multiple languages. Presidio supports Python and PySpark workloads, Docker, and Kubernetes, and includes image redaction for standard and DICOM medical images.
title: Presidio

body: Test your prompts, agents, and RAGs. Red teaming/pentesting/vulnerability scanning for AI. Compare performance of GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, and more. Simple declarative configs with command line and CI/CD integration.  Used by OpenAI and Anthropic.
plain_description: **Evaluate prompts and test AI applications for security risks before release.** Compare model performance side by side and automate checks in CI/CD.
technical_description: Promptfoo is a command-line tool and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM-based applications. It supports automated prompt and model evaluations, vulnerability scanning, model comparisons, CI/CD checks, and pull request code scanning. Evaluations run locally; most LLM providers require an API key.
title: Promptfoo

body: How Python does AI. Agents, realtime voice, image generation, embeddings. Every model, every interface, typed end to end.
plain_description: **Build AI agents that turn business requests into typed, validated results.** Use them for data extraction, customer support, voice interactions, and long-running workflows. Connect the same agent to different models and interfaces.
technical_description: Pydantic AI is a typed Python SDK for building AI agents across model providers. It supports tools, structured outputs, model fallbacks, realtime voice, image generation, embeddings, and integrations for web, CLI, UI, and durable workflows. Pydantic AI Harness adds capabilities such as memory, guardrails, planning, persistence, and coding agents; related packages provide evaluation and graph-based control flow.
title: Pydantic AI

body: Qdrant - High-performance, massive-scale Vector Database and Vector Search Engine for the next generation of AI. Also available in the cloud https://cloud.qdrant.io/
plain_description: **Find and organize information by meaning to power smarter search and recommendations.** Store vector data, filter results, and connect Qdrant to your applications. Run it locally or use the managed cloud service.
technical_description: Qdrant is a vector similarity search engine and database for storing, searching, and managing vectors with payloads. It supports dense, sparse, and multivector search; filtering, hybrid search, recommendations, and vector quantization. It offers REST and gRPC APIs, a Web UI, distributed deployment, a managed cloud service, and Qdrant Edge for local, offline-capable use.
title: Qdrant

body: Qwen3-VL is the multimodal large language model series developed by Qwen team, Alibaba Cloud.
plain_description: **Understand images, documents, and videos with a multimodal AI model.** Use it to recognize objects, extract text and key information, and reason about visual content. It can also help control computer and mobile interfaces.
technical_description: Qwen3-VL is a vision-language model series with Dense and MoE architectures, Instruct and Thinking editions, and model sizes ranging from 2B to 235B. The README shows local inference with Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang; online serving through an OpenAI-style API; and a browser-based demo. Capabilities include image and video understanding, OCR, document parsing, spatial reasoning, and visual agent tasks. The README also documents fine-tuning Qwen2-VL and Qwen2.5-VL.
title: Qwen3-VL

body: text-generation
plain_description: **Use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to generate helpful answers, code, and structured text for your business.** It follows instructions, supports long inputs, and works across many languages.
technical_description: An instruction-tuned 7.61B-parameter causal language model in the Qwen2.5 series. The README demonstrates loading it with Hugging Face Transformers and generating text with a chat template. It supports up to 131,072 tokens of context with configuration for long-text use, and recommends vLLM for deployment.
title: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct

body: Ray is an AI compute engine. Ray consists of a core distributed runtime and a set of AI Libraries for accelerating ML workloads.
plain_description: **Scale Python and AI workloads from a laptop to a cluster.** Use Ray’s libraries for data, distributed training, hyperparameter tuning, reinforcement learning, and serving. Monitor applications and clusters with the Ray Dashboard.
technical_description: Ray is a framework for scaling Python and AI applications. It combines a distributed runtime with libraries for scalable datasets, distributed training, hyperparameter tuning, reinforcement learning, and programmable serving. Ray runs on machines, clusters, cloud providers, and Kubernetes; it can be installed with `pip install ray`.
title: Ray

body: LLM Prompt Injection Detector
plain_description: **Protect your AI applications from prompt injection attacks.** Rebuff checks incoming prompts and detects when canary words leak from prompts.
technical_description: Rebuff is a prototype prompt injection detector with layered defenses: input heuristics, LLM-based detection, vector database comparisons against prior attacks, and canary tokens for detecting prompt leakage. It provides JavaScript/TypeScript and Python SDKs. The README shows setup with OpenAI and Pinecone; self-hosting the playground also uses Supabase and a vector database.
title: Rebuff.ai

body: Easily train a good VC model with voice data <= 10 mins!
plain_description: **Turn a short voice recording into a custom voice model for speech or real-time voice changing.** Train with as little as 10 minutes of audio. Use the web interface to train and run voice conversion.
technical_description: A Python voice-conversion framework with a web interface for training and inference. It uses top-1 retrieval to replace input features with features from the training set, and supports real-time voice conversion and vocal separation through pymss/MSST. The README documents CPU, AMD/Intel, NVIDIA GPU, and Windows DirectML dependency options.
title: Retrieval-based Voice Conversion WebUI

body: The repository provides code for running inference with the Meta Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), links for downloading the trained model checkpoints, and example notebooks that show how to use the model.
plain_description: **Help your team identify and track objects across images and videos.** Use visual prompts to create or refine masks, and track multiple objects through video. Train or fine-tune the model on your own image and video datasets.
technical_description: SAM 2 is a promptable visual segmentation model for images and videos. The repository provides PyTorch inference APIs for image prediction, automatic mask generation, and video segmentation and tracking, plus model checkpoints, training and fine-tuning code, example notebooks, and a locally deployable web demo. Installation requires Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.5.1+, and TorchVision 0.20.1+; a GPU machine and CUDA toolkit are recommended for installation and inference.
title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos

body: YC (S26) | Screenpipe finds the work worth automating | Continuously record computer work locally, discover recurring workflows, and hand the result to any agent you already use.
plain_description: **Find repeated work worth automating by recording computer activity locally.** Review workflows with links to their source captures, then hand them to agents and automation tools you already use. Search screen and audio history for useful context.
technical_description: Screenpipe records screen activity and audio locally, extracts text from accessibility data or OCR, transcribes speech, and stores searchable history on the device. Its desktop app includes a timeline and AI-powered search. Workflows can be reviewed and handed off through MCP, a REST API, the JavaScript SDK, or scheduled pipes. Local capture and search work offline after setup; cloud AI, sync, and connected services require network access. Product analytics is enabled by default and can be disabled in settings.
title: screenpipe

body: An MLOps framework to package, deploy, monitor and manage thousands of production machine learning models
plain_description: **Deploy and scale AI applications across your Kubernetes environments.** Serve multiple models together to reduce infrastructure costs. Route traffic between models or pipelines for A/B tests and shadow deployments.
technical_description: Seldon Core 2 is an MLOps and LLMOps framework for deploying, managing, and scaling AI systems in Kubernetes, on premises or in the cloud. It supports model serving, composable AI pipelines with Kafka streaming, autoscaling, multi-model serving, overcommit, and experiments that route data between candidate models or pipelines.
title: Seldon Core 2

body: Semantic ifs from open models, on a 3090 at home. Independent; not affiliated with Jev or TypeSafe.
plain_description: **Make fast, structured decisions with open models, without waiting for a generated answer.** Supply a state, criteria, and options to get probabilities for each option. Run the browser demo or use the Python scoring tools.
technical_description: SemIf reads typed option probabilities directly from open language models for runtime-defined decisions. It supports Python scoring with CUDA, Apple Silicon MPS and MLX, or CPU via llama.cpp and local GGUF checkpoints. A browser demo runs models with WebGPU. Includes state reuse, calibration, benchmarks, and reproducible evaluation artifacts.
title: SemIf

body: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.
plain_description: **Serve large language and multimodal models for your business applications.** Use SGLang for high performance inference, agentic workloads, and large scale serving. It also includes tools for generating images, video, audio, and actions.
technical_description: SGLang is an open-source inference framework for large language, vision-language, and diffusion models, optimized for agentic workloads, large-scale serving, and reinforcement learning rollouts. Its built-in SGLang Diffusion engine supports image, video, audio, and action generation. The README describes Docker and Python installation, broad GPU, TPU, NPU, CPU, and Apple Silicon support, and deployment integrations.
title: SGLang

body: Silero VAD: pre-trained enterprise-grade Voice Activity Detector
plain_description: **Find where speech occurs in audio so your team can prepare recordings and automate voice workflows.** Works for call centers, voice bots, and edge or mobile use cases. Processes audio locally without telemetry, keys, or registration.
technical_description: Silero VAD is a pre-trained voice activity detector. Its Python package accepts audio and returns speech timestamps. The README documents PyTorch and ONNX options, CPU and GPU execution, and support for 8 kHz and 16 kHz audio. Python examples require at least 1 GB RAM and a modern AVX-capable CPU; ONNX Runtime can support other architectures.
title: Silero VAD

body: LLM Frontend for Power Users.
plain_description: **Give your team one place to interact with many AI text, image, and voice tools.** Customize prompts and the interface, and extend it with community add-ons.
technical_description: A locally installed user interface for interacting with text-generation LLMs, image-generation engines, and TTS voice models. It connects to many LLM APIs and supports image generation integrations, text-to-speech, lorebooks, translation, and third-party extensions. The README says it does not provide hosted services or programmatically track user data.
title: SillyTavern

body: 🤗 smolagents: a barebones library for agents that think in code.
plain_description: **Build AI agents that can carry out multi-step tasks using the models and tools you choose.** Create agents in a few lines of Python and share them through Hugging Face Hub. Supports code-driven and tool-calling agents, with optional sandboxed execution.
technical_description: smolagents is a Python library for building model-agnostic agents. Its CodeAgent writes actions as Python code, while ToolCallingAgent uses structured tool calls. It integrates with Hugging Face inference providers, LiteLLM, OpenAI-compatible services, local Transformers and llama.cpp models, MCP servers, LangChain tools, and Hub tools. Agents can use text, vision, video, and audio inputs. Code execution can run in managed cloud sandboxes or Docker; the built-in LocalPythonExecutor is not a security boundary.
title: smolagents

body: text-generation
plain_description: **Create lightweight AI writing and chat features that run on devices you control.** Use it to rewrite text, summarize content, answer questions, or make function calls. The model supports local use through Transformers or Transformers.js.
technical_description: SmolLM2 is a family of compact language models, with 135M, 360M, and 1.7B parameter variants. The 1.7B Instruct model supports text generation, rewriting, summarization, and function calling. It can be loaded with Transformers or Transformers.js and run on CPU or GPU; the README also provides a TRL terminal chat example. Available formats listed in the repository metadata are safetensors and ONNX.
title: SmolLM2

body: sentence-similarity
plain_description: **Improve multilingual search so people can find the most relevant information across your content.** Generate text embeddings for search and retrieval, with support for English and many other languages. The README describes efficient inference and compact embeddings.
technical_description: A multilingual sentence embedding model optimized for retrieval performance and inference efficiency. It supports an 8192-token context window and Matryoshka Representation Learning at 256 dimensions; the README describes combining vector truncation with 4-bit quantization for 128-byte embeddings. Example usage is provided with Sentence Transformers, Hugging Face Transformers, and Transformers.js.
title: Snowflake's Arctic-embed-l-v2.0

body: SoftVC VITS Singing Voice Conversion
plain_description: **Convert source vocals into a different singing voice while preserving the original pitch and intonation.** Train models on your own audio dataset, then convert vocals with options for pitch, speaker selection, and voice mixing. The README says the project is intended for academic use, not production.
technical_description: An offline framework for singing voice conversion. It extracts speech features from source audio with a SoftVC encoder and feeds them into VITS without converting them to text, preserving pitch and intonation. Users prepare datasets, train models, and run inference; optional features include shallow diffusion, feature retrieval, timbre mixing, and ONNX export. It does not include models or work as a standalone synthesis tool.
title: SoftVC VITS Singing Voice Conversion

body: A PyTorch-based Speech Toolkit
plain_description: **Build speech and conversational AI features for your products.** Use ready-made recipes and pretrained models for transcription, speech generation, speaker recognition, and other audio and text tasks. Train models from scratch or fine-tune existing ones.
technical_description: SpeechBrain is an open-source PyTorch toolkit for conversational AI, speech, and text processing. It provides training recipes across more than 20 tasks, pretrained models with inference interfaces, and support for training from scratch or fine-tuning pretrained models. It also supports GPU and distributed training, Hugging Face integration, and YAML-based hyperparameter management.
title: SpeechBrain

body: Stable Diffusion web UI
plain_description: **Create and edit images from text prompts using a web interface.** Generate variations, inpaint or outpaint images, and upscale results. A training tab supports embeddings, hypernetworks, and LoRAs.
technical_description: A Gradio-based web interface for Stable Diffusion with txt2img and img2img generation, image editing, upscaling, prompt tools, checkpoint management, and training features. The README documents Windows, Linux, and Apple Silicon installation paths, with support for NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, Intel CPUs and GPUs, and Ascend NPUs. It also lists an API and safetensors checkpoint loading.
title: Stable Diffusion web UI

body: text-generation
plain_description: **Help developers complete and generate code from surrounding context.** Trained across 600+ programming languages, it can suggest code snippets and support code generation.
technical_description: StarCoder2-15B is a 15-billion-parameter text generation model trained on more than 4 trillion tokens from The Stack v2 and other selected sources. It uses a fill-in-the-middle objective and supports a 16,384-token context window. The README shows loading it with Transformers on CPU or GPU and describes 8-bit and 4-bit quantization through bitsandbytes. It is not an instruction model, and generated code may contain bugs or exploits.
title: StarCoder2

body: OCR, layout analysis, reading order, table recognition in 90+ languages
plain_description: **Turn documents into searchable, structured information.** Extract text from PDFs and images, understand page layout and reading order, and convert tables into HTML. Supports more than 90 languages.
technical_description: Surya is a 689M-parameter document OCR and layout vision-language model. It performs OCR, layout analysis, reading-order detection, and table recognition, returning structured blocks with labels, coordinates, confidence, and HTML. It runs through vLLM, llama.cpp, or an opt-in MLX backend; the package can start an inference server automatically or connect to an existing OpenAI-compatible server. An interactive browser viewer is included.
title: Surya

body: Self-hosted AI coding assistant
plain_description: **Give your team a self-hosted AI coding assistant to help write and edit code.** Run it on your own infrastructure as an alternative to GitHub Copilot. Connect it to supported code editors and use its OpenAPI interface to integrate with existing tools.
technical_description: Tabby is an open-source, self-hosted AI coding assistant and on-premises alternative to GitHub Copilot. The README describes code completion and chat, editor extensions, an OpenAPI interface, and support for consumer-grade GPUs. It can run as a server using Docker; the example uses CUDA and specifies code and chat models.
title: Tabby

body: The official API server for Exllama. OAI compatible, lightweight, and fast.
plain_description: **Run fast local language models through an API for your applications.** Load and manage models, download them from Hugging Face, and serve concurrent requests. Docker images are available for NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.
technical_description: A FastAPI-based inference server and the official API backend for ExllamaV3. It supports OpenAI-compatible chat completions and tool/function calling, model loading and unloading, Hugging Face downloads, embeddings, speculative decoding, and concurrent inference. Supported model types include Exl3 and FP16/BF16.
title: TabbyAPI

body: TensorRT LLM provides users with an easy-to-use Python API to define Large Language Models (LLMs) and supports state-of-the-art optimizations to perform inference efficiently on NVIDIA GPUs. TensorRT LLM also contains components to create Python and C++ runtimes that orchestrate the inference execution in a performant way.
plain_description: **Run large language models and visual generation models faster on NVIDIA GPUs.** Optimize inference for your workloads. Customize and extend the system with its Python framework.
technical_description: TensorRT LLM is an open-source library for optimizing LLM and visual generation inference on NVIDIA GPUs. It provides custom kernels for common inference operations, runtime optimizations, and a high-level Python API for single-GPU, multi-GPU, or multi-node deployments. It integrates with NVIDIA Dynamo and Triton Inference Server. Telemetry is collected by default, with opt-out options.
title: TensorRT LLM

body: Tesseract Open Source OCR Engine (main repository)
plain_description: **Turn images into searchable text and documents your business can use.** Recognizes text in more than 100 languages and can produce text, PDF, and structured output formats. It can also be trained to recognize other languages.
technical_description: Tesseract is an open-source OCR engine provided as the libtesseract library and a command-line program. Its current stable major version uses an LSTM-based engine for line recognition and also supports the legacy engine. It reads image formats including PNG, JPEG, and TIFF, and can output plain text, hOCR, PDF, TSV, ALTO, and PAGE. It supports UTF-8 and requires traineddata files.
title: Tesseract OCR

body: Pure Javascript OCR for more than 100 Languages 📖🎉🖥
plain_description: **Turn images into searchable text in more than 100 languages.** Use it in a browser or a Node.js application to recognize text from images.
technical_description: Tesseract.js is a JavaScript library that brings the Tesseract OCR engine to browsers and Node.js by wrapping a WebAssembly port. It recognizes text in images and supports workers and schedulers for processing. It does not support PDF files or modify the recognition model.
title: Tesseract.js

body: Large Language Model Text Generation Inference
plain_description: **Serve open source language models to power AI features in your products.** Stream generated text and handle requests at scale. Connect through a REST API, including an API compatible with OpenAI Chat Completions.
technical_description: A Rust, Python, and gRPC server for deploying and serving large language models. TGI supports streamed text generation, continuous batching, multi-GPU tensor parallelism, quantization, and safetensors weight loading. The README says the project is in maintenance mode.
title: Text Generation Inference

body: Open-source desktop app for local LLMs. Text, vision, tool-calling, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API. 100% private.
plain_description: **Run a private AI assistant on your own computer.** Chat with local models, use them through an API, and work with documents, images, and custom tools. Fine-tuning and image generation are also available.
technical_description: TextGen is an open-source desktop app and browser-based web UI for running local language models. It supports GGUF models and multiple backends, including llama.cpp, Transformers, ExLlamaV3, and TensorRT-LLM. Features include chat, image input, document attachments, tool calling, an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API, LoRA fine-tuning, and image generation. The README states the app works offline and has no telemetry.
title: TextGen

body: The Triton Inference Server provides an optimized cloud and edge inferencing solution.
plain_description: **Deploy AI models for inference across cloud, data center, edge, and embedded environments.** Supports models from multiple machine learning frameworks and serves real-time, batched, and streaming requests.
technical_description: Open-source inference serving software for models built with frameworks including TensorRT, PyTorch, ONNX, OpenVINO, and Python. Supports NVIDIA GPUs, x86 and ARM CPUs, and AWS Inferentia; provides HTTP/REST and gRPC protocols, dynamic and sequence batching, concurrent execution, and model ensembles.
title: Triton Inference Server

body: Train transformer language models with reinforcement learning.
plain_description: **Post-train foundation models with reinforcement learning and preference feedback.** Use ready-made trainers or a command-line interface for common training methods. Scale training across GPUs and clusters.
technical_description: TRL is a Python library for post-training transformer foundation models. It provides trainers for supervised fine-tuning, GRPO, DPO, KTO, and reward modeling, plus a CLI. It builds on Transformers and supports distributed training through Accelerate, DDP, DeepSpeed, and FSDP. PEFT integration supports LoRA/QLoRA, and AsyncGRPOTrainer can use a vLLM server for generation.
title: TRL - Transformers Reinforcement Learning

body: Open Source alternative to Algolia + Pinecone and an Easier-to-Use alternative to ElasticSearch ⚡ 🔍 ✨ Fast, typo tolerant, in-memory fuzzy Search Engine for building delightful search experiences
plain_description: **Give customers fast, typo-tolerant search across your products, content, or other data.** Tune rankings, filters, and sorting to shape the search experience. Run it on your own infrastructure or use Typesense Cloud.
technical_description: Typesense is an open-source, in-memory search engine with typo-tolerant keyword search, filtering, faceting, sorting, and vector, semantic, hybrid, and conversational search. It exposes an HTTP API and client libraries, supports self-hosted deployment as a native binary or Docker image, and offers a managed cloud service. The README describes indexing embeddings and using built-in models or external services such as OpenAI for semantic search.
title: Typesense

body: Local UI to run and train LLMs and diffusion models. Supports GGUF, MLX, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4.1, MiniMax-H3, Gemma 4, FLUX and more.
plain_description: **Run and train AI models on your own computer with Unsloth.** Use its desktop app or web UI for language, image, audio, and video models. Fine-tune models and export them for deployment.
technical_description: Unsloth provides a desktop app, web UI, and code-based tools to run and fine-tune language, diffusion, decision, embedding, and audio models. It supports CPU and multiple GPU types, GGUF and MLX models, training methods including LoRA and QLoRA, and deployment through an OpenAI-compatible API or remote and LAN access.
title: Unsloth

body: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
plain_description: **Serve large language models quickly and efficiently for your business.** Handle incoming requests with high throughput and support a wide range of models. Deploy an OpenAI-compatible API server.
technical_description: vLLM is a library for LLM inference and serving. It supports continuous batching, PagedAttention, streaming outputs, quantization, speculative decoding, distributed inference, and more than 200 model architectures. It provides an OpenAI-compatible API server, Anthropic Messages API, and gRPC support, and runs on several GPU types and CPUs.
title: vLLM

body: Vocal Remover using Deep Neural Networks
plain_description: **Separate songs into vocal and instrumental tracks.** Run it on a computer with a CPU or GPU. You can also train a model on your own audio dataset.
technical_description: A Python deep-learning tool that separates an input audio file into instrumental and vocal WAV tracks. It supports CPU and GPU inference, optional test-time augmentation and postprocessing, and training on a user-provided dataset. Installation requires PyTorch and the packages in requirements.txt.
title: Vocal Remover

body: Offline speech recognition API for Android, iOS, Raspberry Pi and servers with Python, Java, C# and Node
plain_description: **Add offline speech recognition to your products and workflows.** Transcribe speech in 20+ languages, create subtitles, and identify speakers. Runs on devices from smartphones and Raspberry Pi to server clusters.
technical_description: An open source offline speech recognition toolkit with models around 50 MB, continuous large-vocabulary transcription, streaming responses, configurable vocabulary, and speaker identification. Provides bindings for Python, Java, Node.js, C#, C++, Rust, Go, and other languages, and supports Android, iOS, Raspberry Pi, and servers.
title: Vosk Speech Recognition Toolkit

body: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
plain_description: **Create videos and images from text or images with Wan2.1.** Generate, edit, and animate visual content, with options for local use through a Gradio demo or integrations such as ComfyUI and Diffusers.
technical_description: Open suite of video foundation models supporting text-to-video, image-to-video, first-and-last-frame-to-video, video generation and editing with VACE, and text-to-image. Includes 1.3B and 14B models, single- and multi-GPU inference, and optional prompt extension using local Qwen models or the Dashscope API. The README gives an 8.19 GB VRAM figure for the T2V-1.3B model.
title: Wan2.1

body: Weaviate is an open-source vector database that stores both objects and vectors, allowing for the combination of vector search with structured filtering with the fault tolerance and scalability of a cloud-native database​.
plain_description: **Find and organize information by meaning to power smarter search and AI applications.** Combine vector search with keyword filters, recommendations, and RAG. Deploy locally or in the cloud and scale as your needs grow.
technical_description: Weaviate is a cloud-native vector database that stores objects and vectors. It supports semantic and hybrid search, filtering, RAG, reranking, and image search through REST, gRPC, and GraphQL APIs. Vectors can be generated with integrated model providers or supplied as precomputed embeddings. Deployment options include Docker, Kubernetes, Weaviate Cloud, AWS, and GCP.
title: Weaviate

body: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
plain_description: **Turn audio into written text and translate speech across languages.** Transcribe audio files from the command line or Python, and identify the language being spoken.
technical_description: Whisper is a general-purpose speech recognition model trained on diverse audio. It supports multilingual speech recognition, speech translation, language identification, and voice activity detection. Install with pip and use from the command line or Python; it depends on ffmpeg and uses PyTorch. Available model sizes have different memory and speed requirements.
title: Whisper

body: Port of OpenAI's Whisper model in C/C++
plain_description: **Turn audio into text with a fast, self-hosted speech recognition tool.** Run transcription on your own computer or device. It supports offline use across desktop, mobile, and browser projects.
technical_description: whisper.cpp is a C/C++ implementation for running OpenAI Whisper speech recognition models. It supports CPU inference and acceleration on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, Apple Silicon, and several NPUs. It includes command-line transcription, streaming, an HTTP transcription server with an OAI-like API, and bindings and examples for multiple platforms. Models use a custom GGML format, with integer quantization support.
title: whisper.cpp

body: A Web UI for easy subtitle using whisper model.
plain_description: **Turn audio and video into subtitles and translated text with a browser-based tool.** Generate subtitles from files, YouTube, or a microphone, then translate subtitle files or add speaker labels.
technical_description: A Gradio browser interface for Whisper transcription, using faster-whisper by default, with options for openai/whisper and insanely-fast-whisper. It supports SRT, WebVTT, and plain text output; speech-to-text translation into English; subtitle translation with NLLB or DeepL; and optional Silero VAD, UVR background music separation, and pyannote speaker diarization. The README also describes Docker and local installation, plus a separate REST API in the backend.
title: Whisper-WebUI

body: WhisperX:  Automatic Speech Recognition with Word-level Timestamps (& Diarization)
plain_description: **Turn audio into fast, searchable transcripts with word-level timing and speaker labels.** Transcribe long recordings in batches and export aligned segments. Run it from the command line or integrate it into Python workflows.
technical_description: WhisperX provides batched automatic speech recognition with word-level timestamps, using forced phoneme alignment and voice activity detection. It supports speaker diarization through pyannote, multilingual transcription, and CPU or CUDA GPU execution. Install with pip or uvx; Python APIs are also documented. Large-v2 can run at up to 70× realtime, and the README notes it requires under 8 GB of GPU memory with the faster-whisper backend.
title: WhisperX

body: Code-first platform for workflows, apps and AI agents, on the fastest self-hostable orchestrator (benchmarked against Airflow, Prefect and Temporal). Business teams build with AI, engineers control what ships. Open-source alternative to Lovable, Retool and n8n.
plain_description: **Build and automate business workflows, apps, and AI agents on one platform.** Business teams can create with AI while engineers review changes before they ship. Scripts can become shareable interfaces, APIs, and scheduled jobs.
technical_description: Windmill is an open-source, self-hostable code-first platform for workflows, apps, and AI agents. Scripts written in 20+ languages can be composed into flows, data pipelines, agents, and full-code React or Svelte apps; they can also generate UIs, API endpoints, and CLI commands. It provides a web IDE, visual flow editor, Git sync, review and promotion between environments, and isolated workers. Self-hosting options include Docker Compose, Kubernetes, and cloud providers.
title: Windmill
